markdown_report:
At 10% progress, select **gated text–ID fusion inside the corrected GRU4Rec** as the first experiment. Benefits remain hypotheses; no experiment was executed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Training separation is already strong. Electronics nevertheless has 4.56% wrong-order comparisons and 7.24% margins below 0.5, making its residual confusion a useful diagnostic target. (2) Users reject broad product associations and overly broad entertainment matches. Item-specific textual details might distinguish these, but shared words can also amplify both failures. (3) Concentration scores near 0.5 imply approximately orthogonal average item directions. They do not justify a collapse penalty or establish recommendation diversity.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [Ask the GRU](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.02116) demonstrates end-to-end text learning through collaborative supervision. Its architecture differs from sequential GRU4Rec, so transfer remains uncertain. (2) [ASIF](https://doi.org/10.1145/3589335.3648308) motivates separating useful shared information from side-information noise. Its alignment machinery should be tested separately from simple fusion. (3) [DenseRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18442) motivates content-to-ID projection. Its pretrained representations provide no evidence that scratch token pooling will succeed here.

**Framework and directions.**

| Direction | Intervention | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Representation | Shared text–ID item vectors | Specificity versus lexical shortcuts |
| Supervision | Same-item alignment | Transfer versus representation distortion |
| Optimization | BPR-max | Hard discrimination versus false negatives |

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Gated text fusion | 3/7/7/6/4 | Minimal test of item-specific information | May reinforce broad similarity |
| Fusion plus duplicate-masked alignment | 4/7/7/6/6 | Explicit cross-view consistency | Adds confounding and false negatives |
| BPR-max alone | 2/6/4/8/4 | Directly targets sampled confusion | Cannot supply missing semantic distinctions |

**Chosen algorithm.** Learn token embeddings and masked-mean title/description pooling from scratch. Project pooled text into the baseline item dimension, then add a small gated residual to each ID embedding. Condition the scalar gate on training-only log frequency and text availability; initialize its weights to zero and bias to −3. Use exactly this representation for history inputs and candidate scoring, retaining the baseline objective, sampler and optimizer.

This explicitly targets **conditionally relevant product matches** and **overly broad entertainment matches** through finer textual distinctions, and targets **Electronics’ sampled ranking errors** through shared representation learning. It cannot establish ownership needs, compatibility, or current intent.

Compare ID-only against fusion first; defer alignment and BPR-max to separate trials. Inspect fixed macro validation HR@10, target-frequency strata, gate magnitude and existing sampled-margin diagnostics. A frequency-bin text-shuffling control can later test item-specific information. Preserve four routes, one selected checkpoint per category, fixed seeds/splits, left-padding correctness, diagnostic interfaces and predictor parity. Training diagnostics and qualitative simulator feedback cannot substitute for pinned validation selection.

idea.description: Add a scratch-trained token-pooling title/description encoder to the supplied corrected GRU4Rec. Fuse its projected output with each item-ID embedding through a frequency-conditioned scalar gate, using the identical fused representation in observed-history encoding and candidate scoring. Train and deploy one jointly trained network per category.
idea.motivation: The selected intervention explicitly addresses two supplied user-facing failures: conditionally relevant products promoted through broad associations, and entertainment recommendations that overgeneralize specific preferences into broad genres or formats. Text may expose more specific distinctions, although it may also amplify lexical shortcuts. The model-facing target is Electronics’ measured 4.56% sampled wrong-order rate and 7.24% small-margin rate, followed by Industrial_and_Scientific’s 3.42% wrong-order rate. These training diagnostics do not establish validation failures or expected gains. The current concentration scores provide no evidence requiring an embedding-collapse penalty.
idea.implementation_notes:
The supplied baseline source is absent from the prompt, so this is an integration specification rather than an invented replacement train.py. Preserve its resolved GRU dimensions, recurrent layers, projections, dropout, objective, sampler, optimizer, batch size and checkpoint-selection schedule for the first experiment. Retain the GRU backbone and corrected padding-state handling.

Use only item titles/descriptions and training histories. Fit the tokenizer/vocabulary using documents belonging to items observed in training; a practical initial configuration is a deterministic lowercase word tokenizer, vocabulary cap 30,000, minimum token frequency 2, token dimension 64, and at most 32 title plus 96 description tokens. These are proposed settings, not measured optima. Use separate PAD and UNK tokens. Missing or token-empty text receives an exactly zero residual. Cache token IDs, not detached learned representations: token embeddings and projection must receive recommendation gradients. Obtain counts from training interactions only, never validation/test targets.

Define text_i = bias_free_projection(masked_mean(token_embedding(tokens_i))). Define gate_i = available_i * sigmoid(a * standardized_log1p(training_count_i) + b), initializing a=0 and b=-3. Standardization statistics come from real training items and are serialized. Define fused_i = id_embedding_i + gate_i * text_i; item zero must remain exactly zero. This starts with a small nonzero contribution and is not baseline-equivalent. Keep all branch scaling and scoring behavior otherwise unchanged. Do not add alignment losses, semantic negative filtering, popularity scores, recency branches or temporal gates in this first trial.

Make the representation accessible consistently: retain the existing item_emb access contract through an embedding-compatible module whose forward returns fused vectors and whose weight access, if required by ModelView, returns the current fused table without detaching gradients. Preserve required attributes such as num_embeddings, embedding_dim and padding_idx where the baseline uses them. Avoid allocating a full differentiable vocabulary table for every sampled training call; gather requested token rows for normal forward scoring. Adapt diagnostic embedding sampling to call the actual fused embedding module. Preserve log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), and all original supported candidate-shape semantics. Both history encoding and candidate scoring must call the same fused embedding implementation.

The existing corrected GRU must skip padding updates or use its established equivalent implementation; zero input alone does not prevent recurrent bias updates. Zero padding features after biased projections. Inference gathers the maximum index where sequence != 0, never count-1, and retains explicit baseline empty-history behavior. No shifted positive target may enter the observed-history encoder.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Honor the host SASREC_EPOCHS setting within that maximum. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing. Save artifacts beneath the trial directory. Use one GPU per trial and account for training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials within 43,200 GPU-seconds. Do not access other trials, hidden tests, extra datasets or pretrained weights.

Save one selected checkpoint per category containing the complete network, token vocabulary, token IDs/masks or reproducible document encoding, training counts/statistics and resolved configuration. Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical model definition and scoring path. Verify fresh predictor loading against the selected in-memory model on identical left-padded inputs and candidate IDs. No averaging or independently fitted score additions are permitted.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), incorporating measured values and definitions. view.model remains the actual nn.Module; keep user_train, meta_data and review_data interfaces without inventing unavailable fields. The loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Measure existing margins through fused log2feats and predict_score. Optional gate means and text/ID residual norm ratios must exclude padding and define denominators. Report unavailable attribute breakdowns as unavailable.

Use the supplied ID-only baseline comparison and this fusion intervention first. If budget remains, separately retrain controls for a fixed gate and text shuffled within training-frequency bins; never fuse their predictions. Select only using the pinned equal-weight macro validation HR@10 and existing checkpoint schedule. Log every attempted setting. Frequency-stratified validation analysis is optional only when the host exposes the requisite outcomes. Neither increased raw margins nor simulator judgments prove compatibility or full-catalog accuracy.
idea.pseudocode:
class FusedItemEmbedding(nn.Module):
    # Instantiate dimensions from the supplied corrected baseline.
    def forward(self, item_ids):
        ids = self.id_embedding(item_ids)
        tokens = self.item_tokens[item_ids]
        mask = self.item_token_mask[item_ids]
        words = self.token_embedding(tokens)
        pooled = (words * mask[..., None]).sum(-2)
        pooled = pooled / mask.sum(-1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1)
        text = self.text_projection(pooled)  # bias=False
        available = mask.any(-1, keepdim=True)
        frequency = self.standardized_log_count[item_ids][..., None]
        gate = available * sigmoid(self.gate_slope * frequency + self.gate_bias)
        fused = ids + gate * text
        return fused * (item_ids != 0)[..., None]

# gate_slope=0, gate_bias=-3; train all network components jointly.
# Replace the baseline's history and candidate embedding accesses consistently.
# Keep its corrected GRU, sample_batch, objective and optimizer unchanged.

DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']
for category in FOUR_SUPPLIED_CATEGORIES:
    set_training_seed(42)
    train_data = supplied_training_split(category)
    vocabulary, token_buffers = encode_public_training_item_documents(train_data)
    counts, count_statistics = training_only_item_counts(train_data)
    model = corrected_GRU4Rec_with_fused_item_embedding(
        resolved_baseline_config, vocabulary, token_buffers, counts, count_statistics)
    for epoch in range(min(resolved_host_epochs, 200)):
        for step in range(200):
            batch = unchanged_family_sample_batch()
            loss = unchanged_baseline_objective(model, batch)
            unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
        unchanged_host_validation_and_checkpoint_schedule()
    save_one_selected_checkpoint_and_all_encoding_state(category)
write_predictor_with_identical_model_and_four_category_routing()
verify_loaded_predictor_score_parity()

def prediction(sequence, candidates):
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
    positions = arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = where(sequence != 0, positions[None, :], -1).amax(dim=1)
    # Apply the corrected baseline's empty-history behavior before gathering.
    return score_final_valid_features_or_handle_empty(model, features, last, candidates)

# Keep DiagnosisProbe and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt signatures unchanged.
# Report actual fused-model metrics; no experiments or gains are asserted here.

originality.positive: Frequency-conditioned text residuals define a focused adaptation within one sequential GRU4Rec, with shared history and candidate representations and a clear attribution experiment.
originality.negative: Joint text–collaborative learning, content projection and gated fusion are established ideas. The novelty is incremental; the supplied references do not establish an exact prior-art boundary.

future_potential.positive: A small representation intervention can test whether training-supervised textual specificity helps sparse items and supports subsequent controlled research on alignment and semantic noise.
future_potential.negative: Scratch text learning may be weak under sparse supervision, descriptions may amplify broad associations, and sampled validation improvements may not transfer to actionable full-catalog recommendations.

code_difficulty.positive: Masked token pooling and a scalar gate preserve fused GRU execution and require no pretrained assets, additional predictor or new training objective.
code_difficulty.negative: Embedding-interface compatibility, efficient repeated candidate encoding, text-state serialization, diagnostic adaptation and exact embedded-predictor consistency require careful integration with the unavailable baseline source.

related_work.title: Ask the GRU: Multi-task Learning for Deep Text Recommendations
contributions: Provides precedent for learning text representations end-to-end through collaborative recommendation and auxiliary metadata supervision.
limitations: Does not implement the required sequential GRU4Rec architecture.
Does not establish that simple scratch token pooling improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: ASIF (2024)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes contrastive ID–side-information alignment and orthogonal decomposition for shared information.
limitations: Does not establish an HR@10 benefit for this GRU4Rec intervention.
Adding its alignment mechanism immediately would confound the first representation-only experiment.

related_work.title: DenseRec (2025)
contributions: The supplied search summary describes projecting pretrained content embeddings into the ID space and examining unseen-item sequence representations.
limitations: Its pretrained content setting differs from the required scratch-trained encoder.
Its reported mechanism cannot be assumed to hold on these fixed Amazon splits.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec implementation
contributions: Provides cross-entropy and BPR-max objectives as relevant GRU-family optimization alternatives.
limitations: Changing objectives does not itself supply item-specific textual distinctions.
Loss and sampling changes should remain separate trials for attribution.
